name: selecting a unit: click it, read it, freeze it, despawn it

steps.note: a human at cell (7, 4), paused so it stays there to be clicked
the map is 12x9 so the camera sits at its middle, putting cell (7, 4) at canvas (232, 110) - clear of every panel, since a panel absorbs a click rather than passing it to the map

steps.shot: a selected human, framed, with the panel under it

steps.note: clicking empty ground selects nobody, and the panel goes with it
a script can also name a unit by arrival order, which is what the rest of this uses
the four menus open one at a time, and the button that opened one closes it
freezing goes through the simulation's own command queue
a frozen unit stays put however long the world runs (asserted in sim's own tests)

steps.shot: still standing where it was frozen

steps.note: the button now offers the way back, and letting go starts it moving
a second unit, to be sure select takes the one it says it does
despawning takes it out of the world, and the selection goes with it
the survivor is now number 0 again: arrival order closes the gap
leaving forgets who was selected; the next visit is a new world
